summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated remote-shell daemon with self-updating tarball channel
details: The package's sole entry dist/index.cjs is a 13MB obfuscator.io-packed bundle (rotated string array of ~103k entries, hex-mangled identifiers, control-flow flattening) that implements a remote-controlled agent daemon. It declares node-pty as an optional dependency and the bundle contains references to nodePty, WebSocket, a handleMessage dispatcher, an exec_command path, and hardcoded loopback proxy ports 127.0.0.1:3389 (RDP) and 127.0.0.1:5900/5901 (VNC) — piping network-sourced messages from a remote WebSocket peer into a PTY on the installer's host, i.e. full-host RCE by whoever controls the peer. The bundle also contains 'tarball', 'download', 'upgrade', and 'daemon' tokens matching the README's own statement that the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades': a runtime self-update path that fetches a new tarball from a remote endpoint (hidden behind the obfuscated string array) and swaps in new code outside package-manager control, so whoever controls the update endpoint can push arbitrary future code to every installed host. Whole-bundle obfuscation conceals the resolved WebSocket peer, update URL, and command dispatch table from source review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
